marks.gloss_en: איתמר נמי: Rava -- to discharge the many, not until an olive's bulk of grain
Rava: even if he dipped with them only in brine and ate with them only one dry fig, he joins
דאמר רב מתנא: אותו היום שניתנו הרוגי ביתר לקבורה תקנו ביבנה הטוב והמטיב
Rav Nachman: Moses instituted for Israel the blessing 'who feeds' at the time the manna came down for them
R' Eliezer: whoever did not say 'a desirable, good and spacious land' in the blessing of the land, and the kingship of David's house in 'who builds Jerusalem', has not fulfilled his obligation
אין לי אלא לאחריו, לפניו מנין? אמרת קל וחומר: כשהוא שבע מברך, כשהוא רעב לא כל שכן -- when sated one blesses; when hungry, all the more so
Grace after Meals is from the Torah: 'and you shall eat and be satisfied and bless' (Deut 8:10)
ברכת התורה מנין? קל וחומר: על חיי שעה מברך, על חיי עולם הבא לא כל שכן -- over temporal life one blesses; over the life of the world to come all the more so
הרי הוא אומר על הארץ הטובה אשר נתן לך, ולהלן הוא אומר ואתנה לך את לחת האבן והתורה -- 'gave' of the land (over which one blesses) and 'I will give' of the Torah (spoken משום רבי ישמעאל)

R' Chiyya bar Nachmani in R' Yishmael's name: it is unnecessary -- it says 'for the good land which He gave you', and below it says 'and I will give you the tablets of stone and the Torah and the commandment' (Ex 24:12)
Rebbi: but the zimmun blessing is derived from 'magnify the Lord with me' (Ps 34:4)
R' Yitzchak: it is unnecessary -- 'and He will bless your bread and your water' (Ex 23:25): do not read uveirakh but uvareikh; and when is it called bread? before one eats it
R' Natan: it is unnecessary -- 'for the people will not eat until he comes, for he blesses the sacrifice; afterwards those invited eat' (I Sam 9:13)
why so much [speech]? because women are talkative
R' Meir: just as one blesses over the good, so one blesses over the bad
R' Yehuda ben Beteira: it is unnecessary -- it says 'good', 'the good': 'good' is Torah, and so it says 'for I have given you a good teaching' (Prov 4:2)
the order of Grace after Meals: the first blessing is 'who feeds'
the Sages' position is the same as the first tanna's
